[1] The ground of the prayer: firm in Śaṅkara-service and contemplation, filled with terrifying Bhairava-power — asmi (I am). [2] Power first invoked against death's gaze, then declared as state. paragraphs.text: Death is looking this way, and the song prays straight at it: O Ender, turn that wrathful, terrible gaze somewhere else — not at me. That is the prayer.

And here is what the prayer stands on: I am steady in serving Śaṅkara and in sitting still with Him in mind, and I am filled to the brim with terrifying Bhairava-power. I am — that is the whole ground. Power gets called in first against deaths stare, and then gets declared as simply the state things are in. (And Śaṅkara here means Shiva, not the philosopher with the similar name.)

paragraphs.text: Death’s gaze turned aside by prayer: O Ender, not toward me with that wrathful-terrible look.
Ground: Śaṃkara-service firm, contemplation steady, terrifying Bhairava-power filling — asmi, I am. Power invoked, then declared as state. Śaṃkara is Śiva here.
